name: TikTok
tagline: Endless algorithmic short-form video feed with creator tools, ads, and in-app purchases.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The app on your phone is a video player with a swipe gesture, which is genuinely a one-afternoon build. The product is a billion people uploading, a recommendation system trained on trillions of watch-time signals, and a CDN that streams vertical video to the entire planet without buffering. A personal replacement has nothing to recommend and nobody to watch. You can absolutely build a local vertical-feed player for your own downloaded videos, and it will feel eerily close for about four minutes, until you run out of content. Nothing you write in a weekend touches the actual machine.
coreLoopDIY: A local swipeable vertical video player over a folder of files you already have, with watch-time logging and a crude re-rank so the loop feels familiar.
requirements: A folder of video files you legally have
A browser that supports HTML5 video and touch or wheel events
whatYouLose: The content: every video, every creator, every trend
The recommender, which is the actual product
Comments, duets, stitches, DMs, and any reason to open it twice
Streaming infra that plays instantly on hotel wifi
Discovery of anything you did not already download yourself
moatNotes: Two-sided: creators go where the viewers are, viewers go where the feed is good, and the feed is good because of watch data from both.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people never pay TikTok a cent, which is the point: the value is entirely the supply of content and the machine that ranks it, and both are funded by advertisers and coin-buyers rather than a subscription. Creators pay in time, brands pay in ad spend, and viewers pay in attention. Nobody is paying for the video player, so replacing the video player replaces nothing.
notes: The swipe feed is a one-sitting build; the feed itself is not. The moat is a billion uploaders plus the watch-time corpus that decides what you see next.
prompt:
Build a local-only vertical video feed player called "soloscroll". Stack: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, better-sqlite3. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no external APIs.

What it does:
1. On startup, scan the directory in VIDEO_DIR (from .env, default ./videos) recursively for .mp4, .webm, .mov files.
2. Index each file in SQLite: id, path, filename, duration, width, height, tags (parsed from the filename, splitting on dashes and underscores), addedAt.
3. Generate a poster frame per video using ffmpeg if it is on PATH; skip silently if it is not.
4. Serve video bytes from a route handler that supports HTTP Range requests so seeking works.

The feed:
- Full-viewport vertical scroll-snap container, one video per screen, autoplay muted on enter, pause on exit, using IntersectionObserver.
- Keyboard (arrow up/down, space to mute toggle), wheel, and touch swipe all move between videos.
- Overlay: filename, tags, a like button, a mute button. That is all the chrome.
- Loop the playlist forever so it never dead-ends.

The fake algorithm:
- Log every view: videoId, secondsWatched, completed, likedAt, timestamp.
- Score each video as (completion rate * 2) + likes - (recent repeats penalty), add a small random jitter, and re-rank the upcoming queue after every 5 views.
- Add a /stats page: total watch time, top tags by completion rate, and your longest session. Be blunt about what that number means.

Explicitly out of scope: uploading, comments, sharing, following, any network calls, any model, any mobile app.

Deliver: .env.example with VIDEO_DIR, a README with setup in under 10 lines, a seed script that indexes the folder, and npm run dev working on a clean clone.
